summary: Client-only request of the 'mon' debug monitor (EocServerMonitor; the Toolkit's option window has a 'ToggleAIShowSubgridEdges' switch, EoC.dll App::AddGlobalSwitchesToOptionDialog). Registered by bg3.exe+0x11EE580 (size 0x10, align 0x10, no destructor = trivially destructible). No system of bg3.exe or of the Toolkit DLLs reads or writes it; the default constructor zeroes both quadwords. Never seen alive.

fields.evidence: default constructor bg3.exe+0x11F08F0 (slot 3 of the ops table bg3.exe+0x5567288 registered by bg3.exe+0x11EE580) stores 0 as a quadword; no other user. Could be an EntityHandle or two 32-bit values - unknown.

fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x11F08F0 stores 0 as a quadword; macOS default constructor also zeroes 16 bytes (stp xzr, xzr).

open_questions: Meaning and real widths of both quadwords: nothing in the shipped binaries fills or reads the request (the monitor implementation is not shipped).
status_reason: no live or captured instance: needs a situation that creates it
second_pass: Cannot be settled from code: the second pass found no producer or consumer anywhere - bg3.exe has only the type registration (App::CreateECS -> bg3.exe+0x11EExxx), the static type-name initialiser and the component ops; the macOS build has only ComponentOps/ComponentSignals/destructor instantiations (macos_index.py names '<mon::' lists just the eight mon types) and the Toolkit DLLs mention them only in App::AddGlobalSwitchesToOptionDialog. The shapes from the creator/destructor stand; the members stay unknown.
